articles.title: Cedar Hollow Gets $850 for Basketball Court
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in July.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 33 weeks once it begins. Harold Rooney, who has lived in Cedar Hollow for 33 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Letters: Sycamore Road Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting.

Please keep the crosswalk in the budget. Many of us on Sycamore Road use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Sycamore Road for 10 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made.
Margaret Orchard, Stonebridge

articles.title: Gloria Lacey, 69, Playground Monitor
articles.deck: Friends remember Gloria Lacey for the many years of service to Upper Commons.
body: Born in Upper Commons in the years after the war, Gloria Lacey spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Gloria Lacey died in December at home on Ridge Place, at the age of 69. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Canal Park Food Pantry in his or her name.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Upper Commons.

articles.title: Then & Now: Keystone Terrace in 1980 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1980 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Keystone Terrace from the corner of Linden Terrace.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1980 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Keystone Terrace from the corner of Linden Terrace.

articles.title: Letters: Chapel Lane Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Chapel Lane for 26 years, and I want to say what a difference the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting.
Please keep the bike repair clinic in the budget. Many of us on Chapel Lane use it every week.
Bernadette Whitcomb, Bellwood
